findings.title: Hundreds of GitHub Repos Compromised By DPRK's PolinRider Campaign
findings.summary_md: OpenSourceMalware first documented PolinRider on March 8, 2026, reporting 675 public GitHub repositories across 352 owners, split between 305 individual users and 47 organizations. The report describes obfuscated JavaScript appended after legitimate content in project config files and a multistage payload culminating in a new Beavertail variant. It attributed the campaign to DPRK-linked activity with connections to Contagious Interview and TasksJacker.

findings.title: North Korean Hackers Publish 108 Malicious Packages and Extensions in PolinRider Campaign
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reported on July 4, 2026 that Socket counted 162 malicious release artifacts covering 108 unique packages and extensions: 19 npm libraries, 10 Composer packages, 61 Go modules and one Chrome extension. It attributed the activity to North Korea-aligned Contagious Interview operators and noted that PolinRider was first flagged by OpenSourceMalware in March 2026. The article said the actors took over maintainer accounts rather than relying only on stolen GitHub credentials, and advised reviewing repository activity logs, package release metadata and VS Code task configuration.

findings.title: GhostAction Crosses Paths With PolinRider: Inside the October Escalation
findings.summary_md: GitGuardian reported that between October 13 and 21 the GhostAction operator pushed 72,026 commits across 22,964 repositories, and that from October 22 to 26 PolinRider loaders were added to 188 GhostAction commits that were then force-pushed. It identified the same Ethereum sender wallet later seen in the npm loaders, 0x1eef0849eda15d87f64e51c73c8442cf3c8bcef3, and listed 95.135.181.151 as fallback C2. The report describes five-stage PolinRider chains that resolve C2 addresses from Ethereum transactions and download XOR-encoded stages from /0x/cls and /0x/ls. GitGuardian said there were no clear indicators that the GhostAction and PolinRider operators were the same.

findings.title: Earliest Known PolinRider Malware Found in 2025 npm Packages
findings.summary_md: OpenSourceMalware traced PolinRider components to nine npm versions published by one maintainer within 90 minutes on May 4, 2025, starting with itsa-utils 1.4.2, with the payload confirmed in four. It found the same XOR key ThZG+0jfXE6VAGOJ, command server 154.91.0.103 and server paths used in later PolinRider samples, alongside JADESNOW, an INVISIBLEFERRET bootstrapper, a Socket.IO RAT and a Python credential stealer. The 2025 samples had the payload and blockchain delivery chain but not the self-spreading behavior documented in 2026.

findings.title: Ethereum resolver wallet behind 95.135.181.151 (4 C2s since Sep 4), plus 2 copies polinrider-scanner.sh misses
findings.summary_md: A public OpenSourceMalware PolinRider tracker issue opened November 1, 2026 records an Ethereum resolver wallet, 0x1eef0849eda15d87f64e51c73c8442cf3c8bcef3, with 205 transactions and four decoded C2 addresses beginning September 4. It lists 166.88.134.75 from September 4, 103.179.143.219 and 23.27.13.72 from October 14, and 95.135.181.151 from October 16. The reporter describes staged downloads from /0x/cls and /0x/ls over port 443, detached node -e processes, and long-line checks in tracked JavaScript files that caught samples a scanner missed.
